findings.issue: Token list opens with two spurious all-null fragments 見 and 失っ (indices 0-1) placed BEFORE われわれ; they duplicate the correctly placed 見失っ+た tokens later and break the surface order of the sentence (token concatenation no longer matches jp).

findings.issue: False orthography claim: ひぎめ IS the standard reading/kana spelling of 日極め (cf. 月極 つきぎめ), so there is no spelling error in the original — it is merely written in hiragana. The note teaches learners a nonexistent error.
findings.current: written entirely in hiragana and with a small spelling error (ひぎめ for 日極め)
findings.suggested: the original is written entirely in hiragana (ひぎめ = 日極め, 'by the day')

findings.issue: Same false claim as expl_en: ひぎめ is the correct reading of 日極め, so 'pequeno erro de grafia' is wrong — the sentence just uses hiragana instead of kanji.
findings.current: escrito todo em hiragana e com pequeno erro de grafia (ひぎめ por 日極め)
findings.suggested: o original está escrito todo em hiragana (ひぎめ = 日極め, 'por diária')

findings.issue: リムジン here means the airport limousine/shuttle bus (en translation: 'shuttle bus'; the token gloss itself says 'airport shuttle van', and sibling sentence 192500 translates it as 'ônibus do aeroporto'). Pt 'limusine' means a luxury stretch car in Brazil — sense-changing false friend.
findings.suggested: Onde fica o ônibus do aeroporto?

findings.issue: Missing space after 'dia' before the parenthesis in the pt gloss of ひ.
試合 is the match/contest, not an opponent; with 勝つ, に marks what is won (contest) or the party beaten. Calling 試合 'the opponent' is a category error (expl_pt hedges correctly with 'oponente/alvo').
findings.suggested: に marking what is won (the match, 試合)
